correctness.rationale: Exact induction on the color partition: for a d-regular H, each product vertex obtains precisely the factor-G neighborhood multiset plus d copies of its own color. Thus the same splits occur and exact stabilization depth is preserved. Connected relatively prime Cartesian products have coordinatewise full automorphism group by the cited Sabidussi–Vizing theory. Product orbit classes are factor-orbit products; equality with lifted color classes is equivalent to refinability of G and transitivity of H. For P_m times C_n, path endpoint waves give depth floor((m-1)/2), while C_n and C_3 disjoint-union C_{n-3} give nonisomorphic products with identical round histograms for n>=6. Standard-library replay passed 405 factor pairs and 80 cylinder cases; these are finite checks only.

value.rationale: The theorem characterizes a natural infinite Cartesian-product regime for exact 1-WL refinement and orbit detection; in addition, it constructs connected refinable yet nonamenable examples with unbounded exact stabilization rounds. This provides a reusable finite-model-theoretic separation of color-type orbits from graph identification, rather than a finite table or arbitrary parameter example.
